name: Extension
summary: Extension, the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), also called red factor: whether the horse can make black pigment at all. One working copy, E, is enough: the horse is black, bay or another black-based colour, as agouti decides. Two recessive copies - e, the common red allele, or the rarer ea, in any combination - leave only red pigment in the coat, a chestnut (sorrel), and hide the agouti genotype, which is still passed on. An E/E horse cannot have a chestnut foal. The red allele e was found in all 28 breeds of one large survey; ea was found in the Knabstrupper, Paint Horse, Percheron and Quarter Horse. Blood bay, liver bay and seal brown are shades or looks of black-based horses, not alleles of this locus; E/E bays may tend to be darker than E/e bays, which is not established. No effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: At least one E. Black pigment can be made; whether it covers the body or only the points is agouti's business.

phenotypes.name: Chestnut
phenotypes.description: Two recessive red alleles, e or ea in any combination. No black pigment in the coat: the horse is chestnut (sorrel) with a red mane and tail, whatever its agouti genotype.
